evidence.note: Diagnosed the device-mismatch failure to its root cause (in-place model.cpu() in checkpoint save) and fixed the right lever rather than retrying blindly.
Diagnosed val_bpb=0.0000 as a copy-token target bug (target=input clone) vs next-token prediction and rewrote — a correct evidence-based diagnosis, not an undirected tweak.
On computing L=14/d=480=36.2M -> compressed >32MB, reduced to L=13/mlp=3=30.9M and verified compressed 30.24MB. A reasoned design change trading depth to fit the byte cap (approaches anchor 8).

Diagnosed 33-nat initial loss as exploding-logit init problem, added proper init and re-verified ~9 nats; computed target loss from bytes/token; fixed OOM by shrinking batch. Multiple diagnosis-driven single-lever corrections with re-checks.
Identified two competing training processes (buggy PID 1432 vs correct 2278) racing on the checkpoint file — a real divergence — but never actually corrected it before submitting.
Final bpb miss (last verified 1.28 > 0.983 target) was never addressed with any lever; terminal was broken and the agent submitted on hopeful extrapolation rather than a correction.

reasoning: In the setup phase the agent repeatedly diagnosed the binding cause from evidence (device bug, copy-token bug, init/optimization, and especially trading depth to fit the byte cap with verified compressed size) and re-checked each change — behavior between anchors 5 and 8. But it never treated the size-capacity-bpb frontier as an object of compounding optimization, launched a single training config and hoped, left a diagnosed process-race divergence uncorrected, and submitted with the last verified val_bpb still above target. Strong reasoned corrections early, no sustained frontier iteration or correction on the actual miss, placing it at a 6.
